pages.title: Spirit Power and Its Value
pages.text: Spirit Power is the essential ability that allows you, as a Saniwa, to summon Touken Danshi.$(br2)When Spirit Power is insufficient, you cannot summon new Touken Danshi.

pages.title: Spirit Power Icon Display
pages.text: Your Spirit Power is displayed in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Keep an eye on the remaining amount.

pages.title: Spirit Power Mechanic: Penalty System
pages.text: Note that Spirit Power is consumed when the player is attacked by monsters.$(br2)Dying triggers a high penalty of 70 Spirit Power deduction, so please act with caution.

pages.title: Spirit Power Mechanic: Saniwa
pages.text: When the player's Spirit Power exceeds 30, the player gains Resistance II, Absorption I, and +8 Armor Toughness.$(br2)When Spirit Power is insufficient, these effects disappear until Spirit Power is restored.

pages.title: Spirit Power Mechanic: Group Anti-Invisibility for Touken Danshi
pages.text: When the player's Spirit Power exceeds 50, the effect [Touken Danshi: Anti-Invisibility] is applied to all Touken Danshi summoned by the player.$(br2)This effect, carried by Spirit Power, grants Touken Danshi the ability to see invisible hostile creatures, allowing them to detect monsters that are invisible.$(br2)When Spirit Power is insufficient, this effect disappears until Spirit Power is restored.

pages.title: Spirit Power Mechanic: Mixed Physical and Magic Damage
pages.text: When the player's Spirit Power exceeds 70, the effect [Touken Danshi: Mixed Damage] is applied to all Touken Danshi summoned by the player.$(br2)This effect, carried by Spirit Power, grants Touken Danshi the ability to deal different types of damage to monsters, dealing both physical and magic damage.$(br2)When Spirit Power is insufficient, this effect disappears until Spirit Power is restored.
